result.summary: This pull request implements predictive prefilling of compact blocks (BIP 152) using transactions reconstructed from previous blocks or extrapools. To prevent redundant round trips at the transport layer, prefilled transactions are capped by the peer connection's available TCP window size. It also adds a cross-platform TCPInfo socket utility to query socket send buffers and window sizes across supported operating systems.
result.problem: Compact block relay currently only prefills coinbase transactions, requiring peers to request missing transactions via a GETBLOCKTXN round trip in roughly 43% of blocks. These round trips slow block propagation network-wide, increasing stale block rates and orphan risk.

resolved_concerns: andrewtoth requested avoiding unnecessary background thread serialization and fine-tuning mutex scopes, which the author addressed.
m4ycon noticed zero-valued size counters in debug logs, which prompted extracting logging improvements into PR 35724.

result.card: This PR improves compact block relay by predictively prefilling transactions that the node needed during its own block reconstruction, while constraining prefill size to the peer's TCP window to avoid extra transport round trips. Empirical testing shows immediate reconstruction without GETBLOCKTXN round trips jumping from 56.9% to 89.7%, substantially speeding up block propagation network-wide without requiring protocol upgrades. The change also adds a cross-platform TCPInfo wrapper in src/util/sock. There is strong concept agreement and positive test reports, with the branch currently rebased on logging dependency PR 35724.
